Accounting for the original 332.35 kg change

Each original month is paired with the same month one year earlier. The symmetric identity allocates -94.56 kg to the published-volume component and 426.91 kg to the load-intensity component. These describe the retained mass/volume values; identifying operational causes requires additional process evidence.

Method and original source context

EPA’s source field guide identifies pollutant load in kilograms per reporting period and wastewater volume in millions of gallons per period. Original average-concentration values and measurement-choice fields are retained separately.

For each matched month, define mass M, volume V and intensity I=M/V. The volume component is (V1−V0)×(I0+I1)/2; the intensity component is (I1−I0)×(V0+V1)/2. Their sum is M1−M0. Summary values add these monthly components. The intensity index describes the ratio of the reported load to published volume.

Temporal aggregation affects allocation. Applying the identity once to Milliken’s whole eight-month window yields -119.12 kg and 451.47 kg. Both approaches retain the same 332.35 kg mass change. Monthly pairing is the primary method; both calculations are saved explicitly.

Inputs are original displayed EPA values under ND=ZERO. Source rounding, missing-value descriptions, qualifiers, QC flags, percentages based on DMRs or limits and original response IDs/pointers travel with each row. A missing or nonpositive volume leaves its accounting pair unsupported. Original historical calendar support remains authoritative.
